notes: §1985:VI.3.2.1.1 prints the division as the header, the PROGRAM-ID paragraph and five optional comment-entry paragraphs, each a paragraph header with its period followed by comment-entries, and §1985:VI.3.2 fixes their sequence ("The other paragraphs are optional and may be included in this division at the user's choice, in order of presentation shown by the general format below."). All of that is implemented at 85 except one arm. Implemented: identificationDivision and identificationBody require PROGRAM-ID first; VersionConformancePass.VisitIdentificationDivision refuses a missing header (COBOL0900); the fixed-form logical conversion (CommentEntryOf) takes an Area-A AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED or SECURITY word in an Identification Division as a paragraph header and discards the entry up to the next Area-A word, so any characters on any number of lines are accepted; the 1985 arm of the ClauseCardinalities row (ByClauseContext, its Earlier figure, in force below 2002) makes ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition refuse a repeated paragraph (COBOL2423) and one out of sequence (COBOL2987); OPTIONS (COBOL0804), REMARKS (COBOL0902), FUNCTION-ID (COBOL0900) and any other paragraph (COBOL1971) are refused. Missing: CommentEntryHeader writes the header as the paragraph word plus '. .' whatever follows the word, so a comment paragraph whose header has no period (AUTHOR JOHN SMITH., or the bare word AUTHOR) is accepted in silence, with no --flag-extensions warning either. §1985:III defines a paragraph header as "A reserved word, followed by the separator period", and §1985:IV.4.2.1 rule 3 allows the period only at a sentence's end "or as shown in formats". docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-CE1 takes the optional period from GnuCOBOL for free form, where no edition speaks; in fixed form at 85 the 1985 format controls. The witness writes AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN and SECURITY with their periods. Probed at --std 85: all five with multi-line entries holding periods, quotation marks and division headers in area B, and all five empty, are accepted; SECURITY before AUTHOR, DATE-WRITTEN after SECURITY, AUTHOR twice, AUTHOR before PROGRAM-ID, no PROGRAM-ID, a missing period after the division header or after PROGRAM-ID or its name are refused.
